definitions.explanation: A crunchy, green vegetable with long stalks and a distinctive aroma, commonly used in salads, soups, and stir-fries.

examples.japanese: セロリ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I put celery in the salad.

examples.japanese: セロリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{苦手|にがて}→苦手：03513_nigate⟧な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many people don't like the smell of celery.

examples.japanese: セロリ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{生|なま}→生：03509_nama⟧で⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{炒|いた}めて→炒める：01879_itameru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{独特|どくとく}→独特：01656_dokutoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{香|かお}り→香り：00189_kaori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{好|す}き{嫌|きら}い→好き嫌い：12206_sukikirai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{分|わ}かれる→分かれる：10976_wakareru⟧。
examples.english: Celery is delicious raw or stir-fried, but its distinctive aroma tends to divide people.

notes:
From English "celery." Also sometimes written as セルリー, though セロリ is the standard modern form. Celery was introduced to Japan in the early modern period but only became popular in home cooking from the mid-20th century onward.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- セロリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧スティック: celery stick
- セロリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{浅漬|あさづ}け→浅漬け：13308_asazuke⟧: lightly pickled celery
- セロリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: celery leaves
- セロリ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{炒|いた}め{物|もの}→炒め物：08537_itamemono⟧: stir-fried celery
